input.rationale: Section 5(a) imposes an unconditional minimum monthly fee for both Hosting Services and Support Services regardless of Client's actual usage, and Section 6 expressly strips Client of any right to documentation for, or to contest, those minimum monthly fees. That is a take-or-pay floor that recurs in each automatically renewing one-year term (Section 13). It fails the fallback on material terms: there is no right to reduce the commitment on 30 days' notice (Client's only exit is whole-agreement termination under Section 14, effective as late as the last day of the month following notice) and no true-up mechanic for underused volumes. The proposal takes the preferred position with two surgical deletions: the fee floor in Section 5(a) is removed so fees are payable only for requested services, and the now-dangling "minimum monthly fees" carve-outs in Section 6 are conformed. Section 3(i) (ordering a credit report on each borrower submitted through the Interface) is a usage-triggered sourcing term, not a minimum volume commitment, and the storage/bandwidth figures in Section 3 are service specifications rather than commitments on Client, so neither is flagged.

proposal.summary: Delete the minimum monthly fee floor and conform the Section 6 references
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We removed the minimum monthly fees for Hosting and Support Services so that Client pays only for the services it requests, consistent with our no-minimum-commitment position, and conformed Section 6 so it no longer references the deleted minimums. If a floor is essential, we could accept one limited to the current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice and trued up rather than penalised.
